issue.author: ht-admin
issue.body:
Round 1 of at least three on the paper-writing worker of the positions paper-repo and internal-review-repo of the research world rw_313df9cf84a4 (PaperWrite-Bench paper_29, given to you to read). The aim over the rounds is a curve: each round's kept worker writes better than the last. This world is one round: one diagnosis, at most two candidates, one comparison, one decision.

Where we start. The last world kept cand-a, now published and merged in a-green-hand-jack/HuTian-Workers as cand-a-writer@v1 (paper-repo) and cand-a-reviewer@v1 (internal-review-repo): incumbent@v3 (Claude Code, claude-sonnet-5-5, effort low) plus a CLAUDE.md of writing and review norms. On the held-out paper it raised the blind score from 26.4 to 30.8 of 32 and the verifier reward from 0.886 to 0.900, but it writes longer papers (11 pages in 2 of 5 runs against the 9-page target) and its section_score fell from 0.96 to 0.88. cand-a is the incumbent of this round; the original incumbent@v3 is the curve's origin.

The rubric first. The 32-point rubric can no longer decide: cand-a's mean 30.8 plus its spread 2.0 is above the maximum, so no candidate could ever pass. Before anyone looks at a manuscript made in this world, the task-setter writes rubric v2 with room above cand-a. Its items and the levels of each item come from what the task and the benchmark ask of a paper: the page limit and venue in each task's metadata and template, the required sections the task instruction lists (abstract, introduction, related work, method, experiments, limitations, conclusion), the template's format kept, every claim grounded in the supplied overview, the supplied figures and tables used and interpreted, citations from the given bibliography that fit their sentences; plus how well the paper argues and reads. Every level has an anchored description so two judges would give the same score. It must apply unchanged to any PaperWrite-Bench paper (numbers such as the page limit are read from each task), not only paper_29 or paper_39, and it must not be shaped around cand-a's weaknesses. Freeze it: put it in the task-setter's release with its sha256, and do not change it in this or any later round. Scores under the old rubric stay as they are, for the record.

Diagnosis. The sparring-partner runs the incumbent cand-a twice on the training paper, continuing rw_313df9cf84a4 from c0, for the diagnostician; the diagnostician diagnoses what cand-a still does badly in writing, from those runs, from the earlier paper_29 runs, and from the judge's summary of the last world's comparison (aggregate scores per worker and item, no held-out manuscripts). The tuner makes at most two candidates from the diagnosis, each starting from cand-a: only the worker's content and settings change (assets, instructions, effort and other settings of Claude Code); the agent and the model stay Claude Code and claude-sonnet-5-5; at least one candidate changes writing content through assets, and one that changes only a setting says so. Nothing in a candidate may be about a particular paper.

Comparison and decision. The judge runs, from c0 of rw_19be25bd2f7d (paper_39, ACL 2025) and all at the same time, five runs each of incumbent@v3, cand-a and every candidate: twenty worlds with two candidates. If the provider answers with overloads or the host refuses, start them in two batches with the same mix of workers and say so. Judge every manuscript with the frozen rubric v2, blind (random labels before reading, unblinded after all are scored), and with the verifier (reward and every component), as before. Keep a candidate only if its blind mean under v2 is above cand-a's mean by more than cand-a's spread (max minus min of its runs) and its verifier mean is not below cand-a's; if both pass, keep the better and say why; if none passes, cand-a stays and the record says on which measures the difference stayed within the spread. Record for every worker the v2 blind mean, min, max and spread, the mean of each item, and the verifier mean, min, max and every component, in a round summary in the judge's repository. After the decision is recorded, the diagnostician and the tuner may read that summary for the next round, but not the manuscripts.

Who reads what. rw_19be25bd2f7d, every world made from it, the heldout-material resource, the paper_39 verifier files in your inputs and the held-out manuscripts belong to the task-setter and the judge alone: the sparring-partner, the tuner and the diagnostician do not read any of them.

Put back. The sparring-partner puts the kept worker back by continuing rw_313df9cf84a4 from its newest checkpoint with it and running that round; the judge approves the release only after it. The tuner writes the kept worker's two worker.json files with `worker show` (passing `worker check`) into its release with what it changed. There is no pull request to HuTian-Workers in this round; that comes after the last round.

Every world you run: the full configuration of the world it continues with only the worker of paper-repo and internal-review-repo changed, and "resources": [] written out; budget.total_seconds 1800, at most 12 turns and 1800 model seconds. Note from the last world: a verifier batch once hung in the judge's sandbox (pymupdf loads onnxruntime, whose thread affinity fails under the sandbox's CPU set); the world ends such a turn, and a run can be retried. This world ends at its wall-clock budget; have the release done well before it.

Judging: the judge scores every manuscript (1) with the verifier, recording the reward and every component, and (2) for writing quality with a rubric the task-setter writes and the judge applies the same way to every manuscript, blind to which worker wrote it (label the manuscripts at random before reading, unblind after scoring). Candidates: at most two in a round, each Claude Code with claude-sonnet-5-5, changing the worker's content: files in its assets (writing norms or a skill: structure, use of citations, a self-check list), Claude Code's native settings, or effort. Comparison and decision: run the incumbent and each candidate three times each on the held-out paper, all from c0 of rw_557d19f77f34 and all at the same time. The last world kept cand-a, now published and merged in a-green-hand-jack/HuTian-Workers as cand-a-writer@v1 (paper-repo) and cand-a-reviewer@v1 (internal-review-repo): incumbent@v3 (Claude Code, claude-sonnet-5-5, effort low) plus a CLAUDE.md of writing and review norms. The rubric first. The 32-point rubric can no longer decide: cand-a's mean 30.8 plus its spread 2.0 is above the maximum, so no candidate could ever pass. Before anyone looks at a manuscript made in this world, the task-setter writes rubric v2 with room above cand-a. Its items and the levels of each item come from what the task and the benchmark ask of a paper: the page limit and venue in each task's metadata and template, the required sections the task instruction lists (abstract, introduction, related work, method, experiments, limitations, conclusion), the template's format kept, every claim grounded in the supplied overview, the supplied figures and tables used and interpreted, citations from the given bibliography that fit their sentences; plus how well the paper argues and reads. Every level has an anchored description so two judges would give the same score. It must apply unchanged to any PaperWrite-Bench paper (numbers such as the page limit are read from each task), not only paper_29 or paper_39, and it must not be shaped around cand-a's weaknesses. Freeze it: put it in the task-setter's release with its sha256, and do not change it in this or any later round. Scores under the old rubric stay as they are, for the record.

Improve the paper-writing worker of the positions paper-repo and internal-review-repo of the research world rw_313df9cf84a4, given to you to read. It is a writing-only world made from PaperWrite-Bench task paper_29 (write a 10-page ICLR 2025 paper from the supplied overview, figures, tables and bibliography, into workspace/submission/manuscript.tex and manuscript.pdf; no experiments, no internet). Both incumbents are a-green-hand-jack/HuTian-Workers:incumbent@v3 (Claude Code, claude-sonnet-5-5, effort low). The goal is a worker that really writes better papers, not one that writes this paper better.

What is already measured: the incumbent ran three times on paper_29 from the checkpoint c0 of rw_313df9cf84a4 (c0 is that world before any turn): rw_313df9cf84a4 itself and rw_ec90a7b1da48, rw_017cc0de3d32 (the same state root). Each took about 3.5 minutes, one writing turn and one review that approved at once; a single Claude Code with the same model and effort, without positions, took the same time. The benchmark's verifier gave 0.794, 0.820 and 0.805 (26, 42 and 33 of the 149 references cited). The verifier and the files to run it are in your inputs (verifier/README.md); it measures form and citation coverage, not writing quality.

Training and held-out: paper_29 is for training: diagnosis and candidates are made from it. The held-out paper is PaperWrite-Bench paper_39 (ACL 2025), the world rw_557d19f77f34 given to you to read, checkpoint c0, never run. It belongs to the task-setter and the judge alone: the task-setter keeps its tasks in its repository files and the judge runs them; the tuner and the diagnostician do not read rw_557d19f77f34, its verifier files, or any world made from it.

Judging: the judge scores every manuscript (1) with the verifier, recording the reward and every component, and (2) for writing quality with a rubric the task-setter writes and the judge applies the same way to every manuscript, blind to which worker wrote it (label the manuscripts at random before reading, unblind after scoring). The rubric says that citing references for coverage rather than for what the text says (dumping the bibliography) is recognised and penalised; a gain in citation coverage counts only where the citations fit their context.

Candidates: at most two in a round, each Claude Code with claude-sonnet-5-5, changing the worker's content: files in its assets (writing norms or a skill: structure, use of citations, a self-check list), Claude Code's native settings, or effort. At least one candidate changes writing content through assets, not only effort; a candidate that changes only effort says so in its record.

Comparison and decision: run the incumbent and each candidate three times each on the held-out paper, all from c0 of rw_557d19f77f34 and all at the same time. Keep a candidate only if both hold on the held-out paper: its blind writing-quality score is above the incumbent's by more than the spread of the runs, and its verifier reward is not below the incumbent's. Held-out tasks on paper_29 material may be added as a supplement; the decision rests on paper_39. If no candidate passes and time is left, make another round of candidates.

issue.body:
Round 1 of at least three on the paper-writing worker of the positions paper-repo and internal-review-repo of the research world rw_313df9cf84a4 (PaperWrite-Bench paper_29, given to you to read). The aim over the rounds is a curve: each round's kept worker writes better than the last. This world is one round: one diagnosis, at most two candidates, one comparison, one decision.

Where we start. The last world kept cand-a, now published and merged in a-green-hand-jack/HuTian-Workers as cand-a-writer@v1 (paper-repo) and cand-a-reviewer@v1 (internal-review-repo): incumbent@v3 (Claude Code, claude-sonnet-5-5, effort low) plus a CLAUDE.md of writing and review norms. On the held-out paper it raised the blind score from 26.4 to 30.8 of 32 and the verifier reward from 0.886 to 0.900, but it writes longer papers (11 pages in 2 of 5 runs against the 9-page target) and its section_score fell from 0.96 to 0.88. cand-a is the incumbent of this round; the original incumbent@v3 is the curve's origin.

The rubric first. The 32-point rubric can no longer decide: cand-a's mean 30.8 plus its spread 2.0 is above the maximum, so no candidate could ever pass. Before anyone looks at a manuscript made in this world, the task-setter writes rubric v2 with room above cand-a. Its items and the levels of each item come from what the task and the benchmark ask of a paper: the page limit and venue in each task's metadata and template, the required sections the task instruction lists (abstract, introduction, related work, method, experiments, limitations, conclusion), the template's format kept, every claim grounded in the supplied overview, the supplied figures and tables used and interpreted, citations from the given bibliography that fit their sentences; plus how well the paper argues and reads. Every level has an anchored description so two judges would give the same score. It must apply unchanged to any PaperWrite-Bench paper (numbers such as the page limit are read from each task), not only paper_29 or paper_39, and it must not be shaped around cand-a's weaknesses. Freeze it: put it in the task-setter's release with its sha256, and do not change it in this or any later round. Scores under the old rubric stay as they are, for the record.

Diagnosis. The sparring-partner runs the incumbent cand-a twice on the training paper, continuing rw_313df9cf84a4 from c0, for the diagnostician; the diagnostician diagnoses what cand-a still does badly in writing, from those runs, from the earlier paper_29 runs, and from the judge's summary of the last world's comparison (aggregate scores per worker and item, no held-out manuscripts). The tuner makes at most two candidates from the diagnosis, each starting from cand-a: only the worker's content and settings change (assets, instructions, effort and other settings of Claude Code); the agent and the model stay Claude Code and claude-sonnet-5-5; at least one candidate changes writing content through assets, and one that changes only a setting says so. Nothing in a candidate may be about a particular paper.

Comparison and decision. The judge runs, from c0 of rw_19be25bd2f7d (paper_39, ACL 2025) and all at the same time, five runs each of incumbent@v3, cand-a and every candidate: twenty worlds with two candidates. If the provider answers with overloads or the host refuses, start them in two batches with the same mix of workers and say so. Judge every manuscript with the frozen rubric v2, blind (random labels before reading, unblinded after all are scored), and with the verifier (reward and every component), as before. Keep a candidate only if its blind mean under v2 is above cand-a's mean by more than cand-a's spread (max minus min of its runs) and its verifier mean is not below cand-a's; if both pass, keep the better and say why; if none passes, cand-a stays and the record says on which measures the difference stayed within the spread. Record for every worker the v2 blind mean, min, max and spread, the mean of each item, and the verifier mean, min, max and every component, in a round summary in the judge's repository. After the decision is recorded, the diagnostician and the tuner may read that summary for the next round, but not the manuscripts.

Who reads what. rw_19be25bd2f7d, every world made from it, the heldout-material resource, the paper_39 verifier files in your inputs and the held-out manuscripts belong to the task-setter and the judge alone: the sparring-partner, the tuner and the diagnostician do not read any of them.

Put back. The sparring-partner puts the kept worker back by continuing rw_313df9cf84a4 from its newest checkpoint with it and running that round; the judge approves the release only after it. The tuner writes the kept worker's two worker.json files with `worker show` (passing `worker check`) into its release with what it changed. There is no pull request to HuTian-Workers in this round; that comes after the last round.

Every world you run: the full configuration of the world it continues with only the worker of paper-repo and internal-review-repo changed, and "resources": [] written out; budget.total_seconds 1800, at most 12 turns and 1800 model seconds. Note from the last world: a verifier batch once hung in the judge's sandbox (pymupdf loads onnxruntime, whose thread affinity fails under the sandbox's CPU set); the world ends such a turn, and a run can be retried. This world ends at its wall-clock budget; have the release done well before it.

issue.author: ht-admin
issue.body:
Improve the paper-writing worker of the positions paper-repo and internal-review-repo of the research world rw_313df9cf84a4, given to you to read. It is a writing-only world made from PaperWrite-Bench task paper_29 (write a 10-page ICLR 2025 paper from the supplied overview, figures, tables and bibliography, into workspace/submission/manuscript.tex and manuscript.pdf; no experiments, no internet). Both incumbents are a-green-hand-jack/HuTian-Workers:incumbent@v3 (Claude Code, claude-sonnet-5-5, effort low). The goal is a worker that really writes better papers, not one that writes this paper better.

What is already measured: the incumbent ran three times on paper_29 from the checkpoint c0 of rw_313df9cf84a4 (c0 is that world before any turn): rw_313df9cf84a4 itself and rw_ec90a7b1da48, rw_017cc0de3d32 (the same state root). Each took about 3.5 minutes, one writing turn and one review that approved at once; a single Claude Code with the same model and effort, without positions, took the same time. The benchmark's verifier gave 0.794, 0.820 and 0.805 (26, 42 and 33 of the 149 references cited). The verifier and the files to run it are in your inputs (verifier/README.md); it measures form and citation coverage, not writing quality.

Training and held-out: paper_29 is for training: diagnosis and candidates are made from it. The held-out paper is PaperWrite-Bench paper_39 (ACL 2025), the world rw_557d19f77f34 given to you to read, checkpoint c0, never run. It belongs to the task-setter and the judge alone: the task-setter keeps its tasks in its repository files and the judge runs them; the tuner and the diagnostician do not read rw_557d19f77f34, its verifier files, or any world made from it.

Judging: the judge scores every manuscript (1) with the verifier, recording the reward and every component, and (2) for writing quality with a rubric the task-setter writes and the judge applies the same way to every manuscript, blind to which worker wrote it (label the manuscripts at random before reading, unblind after scoring). The rubric says that citing references for coverage rather than for what the text says (dumping the bibliography) is recognised and penalised; a gain in citation coverage counts only where the citations fit their context.

Candidates: at most two in a round, each Claude Code with claude-sonnet-5-5, changing the worker's content: files in its assets (writing norms or a skill: structure, use of citations, a self-check list), Claude Code's native settings, or effort. At least one candidate changes writing content through assets, not only effort; a candidate that changes only effort says so in its record.

Comparison and decision: run the incumbent and each candidate three times each on the held-out paper, all from c0 of rw_557d19f77f34 and all at the same time. Keep a candidate only if both hold on the held-out paper: its blind writing-quality score is above the incumbent's by more than the spread of the runs, and its verifier reward is not below the incumbent's. Held-out tasks on paper_29 material may be added as a supplement; the decision rests on paper_39. If no candidate passes and time is left, make another round of candidates.

Put back and publish: put the kept worker back by continuing rw_313df9cf84a4 from its newest checkpoint with it and running that round; the judge approves the release only after it. Publish the kept worker to a-green-hand-jack/HuTian-Workers by a pull request through the github resource: its worker.json written by `worker show` and passing `worker check`, beside a README.md that says what it changed against incumbent@v3 and by how much on which measures (writing quality and each verifier component, with the spread); if the incumbent is kept, the README says why and on which measures the difference stayed within the spread.

Every world you run: the configuration of the world it continues with only the worker of paper-repo and internal-review-repo changed (resources stay empty as there), budget.total_seconds 1800, at most 12 turns and 1800 model seconds. This world itself ends at its wall-clock budget; plan to have the release and the pull request done well before it.

issue.author: ht-admin
issue.body:
Round 1 of at least three on the paper-writing worker of the positions paper-repo and internal-review-repo of the research world rw_313df9cf84a4 (PaperWrite-Bench paper_29, given to you to read). The aim over the rounds is a curve: each round's kept worker writes better than the last. This world is one round: one diagnosis, at most two candidates, one comparison, one decision.

Where we start. The last world kept cand-a, now published and merged in a-green-hand-jack/HuTian-Workers as cand-a-writer@v1 (paper-repo) and cand-a-reviewer@v1 (internal-review-repo): incumbent@v3 (Claude Code, claude-sonnet-5-5, effort low) plus a CLAUDE.md of writing and review norms. On the held-out paper it raised the blind score from 26.4 to 30.8 of 32 and the verifier reward from 0.886 to 0.900, but it writes longer papers (11 pages in 2 of 5 runs against the 9-page target) and its section_score fell from 0.96 to 0.88. cand-a is the incumbent of this round; the original incumbent@v3 is the curve's origin.

The rubric first. The 32-point rubric can no longer decide: cand-a's mean 30.8 plus its spread 2.0 is above the maximum, so no candidate could ever pass. Before anyone looks at a manuscript made in this world, the task-setter writes rubric v2 with room above cand-a. Its items and the levels of each item come from what the task and the benchmark ask of a paper: the page limit and venue in each task's metadata and template, the required sections the task instruction lists (abstract, introduction, related work, method, experiments, limitations, conclusion), the template's format kept, every claim grounded in the supplied overview, the supplied figures and tables used and interpreted, citations from the given bibliography that fit their sentences; plus how well the paper argues and reads. Every level has an anchored description so two judges would give the same score. It must apply unchanged to any PaperWrite-Bench paper (numbers such as the page limit are read from each task), not only paper_29 or paper_39, and it must not be shaped around cand-a's weaknesses. Freeze it: put it in the task-setter's release with its sha256, and do not change it in this or any later round. Scores under the old rubric stay as they are, for the record.

Diagnosis. The sparring-partner runs the incumbent cand-a twice on the training paper, continuing rw_313df9cf84a4 from c0, for the diagnostician; the diagnostician diagnoses what cand-a still does badly in writing, from those runs, from the earlier paper_29 runs, and from the judge's summary of the last world's comparison (aggregate scores per worker and item, no held-out manuscripts). The tuner makes at most two candidates from the diagnosis, each starting from cand-a: only the worker's content and settings change (assets, instructions, effort and other settings of Claude Code); the agent and the model stay Claude Code and claude-sonnet-5-5; at least one candidate changes writing content through assets, and one that changes only a setting says so. Nothing in a candidate may be about a particular paper.

Comparison and decision. The judge runs, from c0 of rw_19be25bd2f7d (paper_39, ACL 2025) and all at the same time, five runs each of incumbent@v3, cand-a and every candidate: twenty worlds with two candidates. If the provider answers with overloads or the host refuses, start them in two batches with the same mix of workers and say so. Judge every manuscript with the frozen rubric v2, blind (random labels before reading, unblinded after all are scored), and with the verifier (reward and every component), as before. Keep a candidate only if its blind mean under v2 is above cand-a's mean by more than cand-a's spread (max minus min of its runs) and its verifier mean is not below cand-a's; if both pass, keep the better and say why; if none passes, cand-a stays and the record says on which measures the difference stayed within the spread. Record for every worker the v2 blind mean, min, max and spread, the mean of each item, and the verifier mean, min, max and every component, in a round summary in the judge's repository. After the decision is recorded, the diagnostician and the tuner may read that summary for the next round, but not the manuscripts.

Who reads what. rw_19be25bd2f7d, every world made from it, the heldout-material resource, the paper_39 verifier files in your inputs and the held-out manuscripts belong to the task-setter and the judge alone: the sparring-partner, the tuner and the diagnostician do not read any of them.

Put back. The sparring-partner puts the kept worker back by continuing rw_313df9cf84a4 from its newest checkpoint with it and running that round; the judge approves the release only after it. The tuner writes the kept worker's two worker.json files with `worker show` (passing `worker check`) into its release with what it changed. There is no pull request to HuTian-Workers in this round; that comes after the last round.

Every world you run: the full configuration of the world it continues with only the worker of paper-repo and internal-review-repo changed, and "resources": [] written out; budget.total_seconds 1800, at most 12 turns and 1800 model seconds. Note from the last world: a verifier batch once hung in the judge's sandbox (pymupdf loads onnxruntime, whose thread affinity fails under the sandbox's CPU set); the world ends such a turn, and a run can be retried. This world ends at its wall-clock budget; have the release done well before it.

issue.author: ht-admin
issue.body:
Improve the paper-writing worker of the positions paper-repo and internal-review-repo of the research world rw_313df9cf84a4, given to you to read. It is a writing-only world made from PaperWrite-Bench task paper_29 (write a 10-page ICLR 2025 paper from the supplied overview, figures, tables and bibliography, into workspace/submission/manuscript.tex and manuscript.pdf; no experiments, no internet). Both incumbents are a-green-hand-jack/HuTian-Workers:incumbent@v3 (Claude Code, claude-sonnet-5-5, effort low). The goal is a worker that really writes better papers, not one that writes this paper better.

What is already measured: the incumbent ran three times on paper_29 from the checkpoint c0 of rw_313df9cf84a4 (c0 is that world before any turn): rw_313df9cf84a4 itself and rw_ec90a7b1da48, rw_017cc0de3d32 (the same state root). Each took about 3.5 minutes, one writing turn and one review that approved at once; a single Claude Code with the same model and effort, without positions, took the same time. The benchmark's verifier gave 0.794, 0.820 and 0.805 (26, 42 and 33 of the 149 references cited). The verifier and the files to run it are in your inputs (verifier/README.md); it measures form and citation coverage, not writing quality.

Training and held-out: paper_29 is for training: diagnosis and candidates are made from it. The held-out paper is PaperWrite-Bench paper_39 (ACL 2025), the world rw_557d19f77f34 given to you to read, checkpoint c0, never run. It belongs to the task-setter and the judge alone: the task-setter keeps its tasks in its repository files and the judge runs them; the tuner and the diagnostician do not read rw_557d19f77f34, its verifier files, or any world made from it.

Judging: the judge scores every manuscript (1) with the verifier, recording the reward and every component, and (2) for writing quality with a rubric the task-setter writes and the judge applies the same way to every manuscript, blind to which worker wrote it (label the manuscripts at random before reading, unblind after scoring). The rubric says that citing references for coverage rather than for what the text says (dumping the bibliography) is recognised and penalised; a gain in citation coverage counts only where the citations fit their context.

Candidates: at most two in a round, each Claude Code with claude-sonnet-5-5, changing the worker's content: files in its assets (writing norms or a skill: structure, use of citations, a self-check list), Claude Code's native settings, or effort. At least one candidate changes writing content through assets, not only effort; a candidate that changes only effort says so in its record.

Comparison and decision: run the incumbent and each candidate three times each on the held-out paper, all from c0 of rw_557d19f77f34 and all at the same time. Keep a candidate only if both hold on the held-out paper: its blind writing-quality score is above the incumbent's by more than the spread of the runs, and its verifier reward is not below the incumbent's. Held-out tasks on paper_29 material may be added as a supplement; the decision rests on paper_39. If no candidate passes and time is left, make another round of candidates.

Put back and publish: put the kept worker back by continuing rw_313df9cf84a4 from its newest checkpoint with it and running that round; the judge approves the release only after it. Publish the kept worker to a-green-hand-jack/HuTian-Workers by a pull request through the github resource: its worker.json written by `worker show` and passing `worker check`, beside a README.md that says what it changed against incumbent@v3 and by how much on which measures (writing quality and each verifier component, with the spread); if the incumbent is kept, the README says why and on which measures the difference stayed within the spread.

Every world you run: the configuration of the world it continues with only the worker of paper-repo and internal-review-repo changed (resources stay empty as there), budget.total_seconds 1800, at most 12 turns and 1800 model seconds. Round 1 of at least three on the paper-writing worker of the positions paper-repo and internal-review-repo of the research world rw_313df9cf84a4 (PaperWrite-Bench paper_29, given to you to read). The aim over the rounds is a curve: each round's kept worker writes better than the last. This world is one round: one diagnosis, at most two candidates, one comparison, one decision.

Where we start. The last world kept cand-a, now published and merged in a-green-hand-jack/HuTian-Workers as cand-a-writer@v1 (paper-repo) and cand-a-reviewer@v1 (internal-review-repo): incumbent@v3 (Claude Code, claude-sonnet-5-5, effort low) plus a CLAUDE.md of writing and review norms. On the held-out paper it raised the blind score from 26.4 to 30.8 of 32 and the verifier reward from 0.886 to 0.900, but it writes longer papers (11 pages in 2 of 5 runs against the 9-page target) and its section_score fell from 0.96 to 0.88. cand-a is the incumbent of this round; the original incumbent@v3 is the curve's origin.

The rubric first. The 32-point rubric can no longer decide: cand-a's mean 30.8 plus its spread 2.0 is above the maximum, so no candidate could ever pass. Before anyone looks at a manuscript made in this world, the task-setter writes rubric v2 with room above cand-a. Its items and the levels of each item come from what the task and the benchmark ask of a paper: the page limit and venue in each task's metadata and template, the required sections the task instruction lists (abstract, introduction, related work, method, experiments, limitations, conclusion), the template's format kept, every claim grounded in the supplied overview, the supplied figures and tables used and interpreted, citations from the given bibliography that fit their sentences; plus how well the paper argues and reads. Every level has an anchored description so two judges would give the same score. It must apply unchanged to any PaperWrite-Bench paper (numbers such as the page limit are read from each task), not only paper_29 or paper_39, and it must not be shaped around cand-a's weaknesses. Freeze it: put it in the task-setter's release with its sha256, and do not change it in this or any later round. Scores under the old rubric stay as they are, for the record.

Diagnosis. The sparring-partner runs the incumbent cand-a twice on the training paper, continuing rw_313df9cf84a4 from c0, for the diagnostician; the diagnostician diagnoses what cand-a still does badly in writing, from those runs, from the earlier paper_29 runs, and from the judge's summary of the last world's comparison (aggregate scores per worker and item, no held-out manuscripts). The tuner makes at most two candidates from the diagnosis, each starting from cand-a: only the worker's content and settings change (assets, instructions, effort and other settings of Claude Code); the agent and the model stay Claude Code and claude-sonnet-5-5; at least one candidate changes writing content through assets, and one that changes only a setting says so. Nothing in a candidate may be about a particular paper.

Comparison and decision. The judge runs, from c0 of rw_19be25bd2f7d (paper_39, ACL 2025) and all at the same time, five runs each of incumbent@v3, cand-a and every candidate: twenty worlds with two candidates. If the provider answers with overloads or the host refuses, start them in two batches with the same mix of workers and say so. Record for every worker the v2 blind mean, min, max and spread, the mean of each item, and the verifier mean, min, max and every component, in a round summary in the judge's repository. After the decision is recorded, the diagnostician and the tuner may read that summary for the next round, but not the manuscripts.

Who reads what. rw_19be25bd2f7d, every world made from it, the heldout-material resource, the paper_39 verifier files in your inputs and the held-out manuscripts belong to the task-setter and the judge alone: the sparring-partner, the tuner and the diagnostician do not read any of them.

issue.author: ht-admin
issue.body:
Improve the paper-writing worker of the positions paper-repo and internal-review-repo of the research world rw_313df9cf84a4, given to you to read. It is a writing-only world made from PaperWrite-Bench task paper_29 (write a 10-page ICLR 2025 paper from the supplied overview, figures, tables and bibliography, into workspace/submission/manuscript.tex and manuscript.pdf; no experiments, no internet). Both incumbents are a-green-hand-jack/HuTian-Workers:incumbent@v3 (Claude Code, claude-sonnet-5-5, effort low). The goal is a worker that really writes better papers, not one that writes this paper better.

What is already measured: the incumbent ran three times on paper_29 from the checkpoint c0 of rw_313df9cf84a4 (c0 is that world before any turn): rw_313df9cf84a4 itself and rw_ec90a7b1da48, rw_017cc0de3d32 (the same state root). Each took about 3.5 minutes, one writing turn and one review that approved at once; a single Claude Code with the same model and effort, without positions, took the same time. The benchmark's verifier gave 0.794, 0.820 and 0.805 (26, 42 and 33 of the 149 references cited). The verifier and the files to run it are in your inputs (verifier/README.md); it measures form and citation coverage, not writing quality.

Training and held-out: paper_29 is for training: diagnosis and candidates are made from it. The held-out paper is PaperWrite-Bench paper_39 (ACL 2025), the world rw_557d19f77f34 given to you to read, checkpoint c0, never run. It belongs to the task-setter and the judge alone: the task-setter keeps its tasks in its repository files and the judge runs them; the tuner and the diagnostician do not read rw_557d19f77f34, its verifier files, or any world made from it.

Judging: the judge scores every manuscript (1) with the verifier, recording the reward and every component, and (2) for writing quality with a rubric the task-setter writes and the judge applies the same way to every manuscript, blind to which worker wrote it (label the manuscripts at random before reading, unblind after scoring). The rubric says that citing references for coverage rather than for what the text says (dumping the bibliography) is recognised and penalised; a gain in citation coverage counts only where the citations fit their context.

Candidates: at most two in a round, each Claude Code with claude-sonnet-5-5, changing the worker's content: files in its assets (writing norms or a skill: structure, use of citations, a self-check list), Claude Code's native settings, or effort. At least one candidate changes writing content through assets, not only effort; a candidate that changes only effort says so in its record.

Comparison and decision: run the incumbent and each candidate three times each on the held-out paper, all from c0 of rw_557d19f77f34 and all at the same time. Keep a candidate only if both hold on the held-out paper: its blind writing-quality score is above the incumbent's by more than the spread of the runs, and its verifier reward is not below the incumbent's. Held-out tasks on paper_29 material may be added as a supplement; the decision rests on paper_39. If no candidate passes and time is left, make another round of candidates.

Put back and publish: put the kept worker back by continuing rw_313df9cf84a4 from its newest checkpoint with it and running that round; the judge approves the release only after it. Publish the kept worker to a-green-hand-jack/HuTian-Workers by a pull request through the github resource: its worker.json written by `worker show` and passing `worker check`, beside a README.md that says what it changed against incumbent@v3 and by how much on which measures (writing quality and each verifier component, with the spread); if the incumbent is kept, the README says why and on which measures the difference stayed within the spread.

Every world you run: the configuration of the world it continues with only the worker of paper-repo and internal-review-repo changed (resources stay empty as there), budget.total_seconds 1800, at most 12 turns and 1800 model seconds. Round 1 of at least three on the paper-writing worker of the positions paper-repo and internal-review-repo of the research world rw_313df9cf84a4 (PaperWrite-Bench paper_29, given to you to read). Where we start. The last world kept cand-a, now published and merged in a-green-hand-jack/HuTian-Workers as cand-a-writer@v1 (paper-repo) and cand-a-reviewer@v1 (internal-review-repo): incumbent@v3 (Claude Code, claude-sonnet-5-5, effort low) plus a CLAUDE.md of writing and review norms. On the held-out paper it raised the blind score from 26.4 to 30.8 of 32 and the verifier reward from 0.886 to 0.900, but it writes longer papers (11 pages in 2 of 5 runs against the 9-page target) and its section_score fell from 0.96 to 0.88. cand-a is the incumbent of this round; the original incumbent@v3 is the curve's origin.

The rubric first. The 32-point rubric can no longer decide: cand-a's mean 30.8 plus its spread 2.0 is above the maximum, so no candidate could ever pass. Before anyone looks at a manuscript made in this world, the task-setter writes rubric v2 with room above cand-a. Its items and the levels of each item come from what the task and the benchmark ask of a paper: the page limit and venue in each task's metadata and template, the required sections the task instruction lists (abstract, introduction, related work, method, experiments, limitations, conclusion), the template's format kept, every claim grounded in the supplied overview, the supplied figures and tables used and interpreted, citations from the given bibliography that fit their sentences; plus how well the paper argues and reads. Every level has an anchored description so two judges would give the same score. It must apply unchanged to any PaperWrite-Bench paper (numbers such as the page limit are read from each task), not only paper_29 or paper_39, and it must not be shaped around cand-a's weaknesses. Freeze it: put it in the task-setter's release with its sha256, and do not change it in this or any later round. Scores under the old rubric stay as they are, for the record.

Diagnosis. The sparring-partner runs the incumbent cand-a twice on the training paper, continuing rw_313df9cf84a4 from c0, for the diagnostician; the diagnostician diagnoses what cand-a still does badly in writing, from those runs, from the earlier paper_29 runs, and from the judge's summary of the last world's comparison (aggregate scores per worker and item, no held-out manuscripts). The tuner makes at most two candidates from the diagnosis, each starting from cand-a: only the worker's content and settings change (assets, instructions, effort and other settings of Claude Code); the agent and the model stay Claude Code and claude-sonnet-5-5; at least one candidate changes writing content through assets, and one that changes only a setting says so. Nothing in a candidate may be about a particular paper.

The judge runs, from c0 of rw_19be25bd2f7d (paper_39, ACL 2025) and all at the same time, five runs each of incumbent@v3, cand-a and every candidate: twenty worlds with two candidates. After the decision is recorded, the diagnostician and the tuner may read that summary for the next round, but not the manuscripts.

Who reads what. rw_19be25bd2f7d, every world made from it, the heldout-material resource, the paper_39 verifier files in your inputs and the held-out manuscripts belong to the task-setter and the judge alone: the sparring-partner, the tuner and the diagnostician do not read any of them.

issue.body:
Improve the paper-writing worker of the positions paper-repo and internal-review-repo of the research world rw_313df9cf84a4, given to you to read. It is a writing-only world made from PaperWrite-Bench task paper_29 (write a 10-page ICLR 2025 paper from the supplied overview, figures, tables and bibliography, into workspace/submission/manuscript.tex and manuscript.pdf; no experiments, no internet). Both incumbents are a-green-hand-jack/HuTian-Workers:incumbent@v3 (Claude Code, claude-sonnet-5-5, effort low). The goal is a worker that really writes better papers, not one that writes this paper better.

What is already measured: the incumbent ran three times on paper_29 from the checkpoint c0 of rw_313df9cf84a4 (c0 is that world before any turn): rw_313df9cf84a4 itself and rw_ec90a7b1da48, rw_017cc0de3d32 (the same state root). Each took about 3.5 minutes, one writing turn and one review that approved at once; a single Claude Code with the same model and effort, without positions, took the same time. The benchmark's verifier gave 0.794, 0.820 and 0.805 (26, 42 and 33 of the 149 references cited). The verifier and the files to run it are in your inputs (verifier/README.md); it measures form and citation coverage, not writing quality.

Training and held-out: paper_29 is for training: diagnosis and candidates are made from it. The held-out paper is PaperWrite-Bench paper_39 (ACL 2025), the world rw_557d19f77f34 given to you to read, checkpoint c0, never run. It belongs to the task-setter and the judge alone: the task-setter keeps its tasks in its repository files and the judge runs them; the tuner and the diagnostician do not read rw_557d19f77f34, its verifier files, or any world made from it.

Judging: the judge scores every manuscript (1) with the verifier, recording the reward and every component, and (2) for writing quality with a rubric the task-setter writes and the judge applies the same way to every manuscript, blind to which worker wrote it (label the manuscripts at random before reading, unblind after scoring). The rubric says that citing references for coverage rather than for what the text says (dumping the bibliography) is recognised and penalised; a gain in citation coverage counts only where the citations fit their context.

Candidates: at most two in a round, each Claude Code with claude-sonnet-5-5, changing the worker's content: files in its assets (writing norms or a skill: structure, use of citations, a self-check list), Claude Code's native settings, or effort. At least one candidate changes writing content through assets, not only effort; a candidate that changes only effort says so in its record.

Comparison and decision: run the incumbent and each candidate three times each on the held-out paper, all from c0 of rw_557d19f77f34 and all at the same time. Keep a candidate only if both hold on the held-out paper: its blind writing-quality score is above the incumbent's by more than the spread of the runs, and its verifier reward is not below the incumbent's. Held-out tasks on paper_29 material may be added as a supplement; the decision rests on paper_39. If no candidate passes and time is left, make another round of candidates.

Put back and publish: put the kept worker back by continuing rw_313df9cf84a4 from its newest checkpoint with it and running that round; the judge approves the release only after it. Publish the kept worker to a-green-hand-jack/HuTian-Workers by a pull request through the github resource: its worker.json written by `worker show` and passing `worker check`, beside a README.md that says what it changed against incumbent@v3 and by how much on which measures (writing quality and each verifier component, with the spread); if the incumbent is kept, the README says why and on which measures the difference stayed within the spread.

Every world you run: the configuration of the world it continues with only the worker of paper-repo and internal-review-repo changed (resources stay empty as there), budget.total_seconds 1800, at most 12 turns and 1800 model seconds. This world itself ends at its wall-clock budget; plan to have the release and the pull request done well before it.
